### 304, 316 and 17-4PH: different heat-treatment questions
Source: https://precision-custom-fasteners-yang.boldshrew261.chatgpt.site/blog/stainless-screw-heat-treatment-grades/
Last modified: 2026-10-29

MATERIALS & FINISHES / 2 MIN READ

### 304, 316 and 17-4PH: different heat-treatment questions

Stainless steel describes several material families. Specify the grade and final condition rather than writing one generic heat-treatment instruction.

By Theo Wan • ZUFEK Technical Editorial • Published October 29, 2026 Material-Specific Heat Treatment

IN THIS GUIDE Distinguish austenitic from precipitation-hardening grades State the purpose of solution treatment Define the final condition of 17-4PH Coordinate finish and verification Resolve what the drawing means by high-strength stainless Separate material treatment from surface treatment Review assembly galling as a separate mechanism RELATED PRODUCT Custom Metal Screws ↗

#### Distinguish austenitic from precipitation-hardening grades

304 and 316 are austenitic stainless steels and are not hardened by the precipitation-aging treatment used for 17-4PH. They can strengthen through cold work, which must be considered separately from heat treatment.

#### State the purpose of solution treatment

Solution annealing and stress-related treatments have material-specific purposes and can affect corrosion behavior and dimensional condition. They should not be treated as a universal hardening cycle.

Working on this type of part? Explore our custom metal screws and include the functional requirements in your RFQ.

#### Define the final condition of 17-4PH

A precipitation-hardening grade requires an explicitly selected condition and corresponding property requirements. Do not assume that any aging cycle is interchangeable with another.

#### Coordinate finish and verification

Passivation is a surface treatment, not the same operation as solution treatment or precipitation hardening. State material evidence, final properties, critical dimensions and requested inspection records.

#### Resolve what the drawing means by high-strength stainless

Clarify whether the requirement names a finished fastener class or a specific alloy and condition. A change from an austenitic grade to 17-4PH changes the material specification as well as the treatment discussion. It needs approval against corrosion, mechanical and application requirements; it is not a manufacturing shortcut to apply without the designer.

#### Separate material treatment from surface treatment

Passivation addresses surface condition; it is not a replacement for the specified material condition. Keep material evidence, mechanical requirements and the surface process separately identifiable in the order. A visually similar surface does not prove that the correct alloy or final condition was supplied.

#### Review assembly galling as a separate mechanism

A selected stainless grade does not eliminate the need to review thread contact and the mating pair. Surface condition, assembly and lubrication can affect galling, and a lubrication change can also affect tightening behavior. Coordinate the assembly process with the approved specification instead of using an unqualified torque figure from another joint.

### Shoulder fits, thread classes and when grinding matters
Source: https://precision-custom-fasteners-yang.boldshrew261.chatgpt.site/blog/shoulder-fit-thread-class-grinding/
Last modified: 2026-10-29

DESIGN & DIMENSIONS / 2 MIN READ

### Shoulder fits, thread classes and when grinding matters

A shaft fit and a thread tolerance class control different interfaces. Write the required function clearly before deciding how the surfaces must be finished.

By Theo Wan • ZUFEK Technical Editorial • Published October 29, 2026 Secondary & Precision Operations

IN THIS GUIDE Separate the plain shoulder and the thread Identify the mating relationship Specify grinding only with a reason Inspect after the relevant finishing stage Compare limits against the actual mating bore Make finishing selection a capability discussion Retain independent acceptance checks RELATED PRODUCT Shoulder & Step Screws ↗

#### Separate the plain shoulder and the thread

A shaft tolerance such as g6 or h7 describes a plain cylindrical feature. A designation such as 6g or 6H belongs to a metric thread tolerance system. Case and order matter; these are not interchangeable callouts.

#### Identify the mating relationship

Provide the mating bore, shoulder length, datums and surface texture. Clearance, locating behavior and rotation depend on both components and their operating conditions.

Working on this type of part? Explore our shoulder & step screws and include the functional requirements in your RFQ.

#### Specify grinding only with a reason

Grinding can be useful for size, form and surface finish, especially after a treatment that changes dimensions. A tolerance designation alone does not prove that centerless grinding is the only acceptable route.

#### Inspect after the relevant finishing stage

Review coating allowance and final condition. Agree measurement methods for size, form and datum relationships, together with thread gauging and the required inspection records.

#### Compare limits against the actual mating bore

Record the shoulder requirement beside the bore limits and operating purpose. Decide whether the joint needs clearance, location or motion and what acceptance condition applies. A shaft tolerance designation and a metric thread class refer to different features. Copying a thread class onto a plain shoulder does not describe the required fit.

#### Make finishing selection a capability discussion

Ask how the proposed route achieves size, form and surface requirements in the final condition. If heat treatment or coating follows an earlier size operation, consider its effect before approving the route. Grinding may be appropriate; the mere presence of a grinding operation does not prove that the specified relationship or finish has been achieved.

#### Retain independent acceptance checks

Check the shoulder using a suitable dimensional method and the thread using the applicable thread acceptance method. Where runout or another datum relationship is specified, verify that relationship directly. Do not substitute a diameter-only screen for a geometry requirement that the screen has not been shown to measure.

### How to specify a tamper-resistant screw drive
Source: https://precision-custom-fasteners-yang.boldshrew261.chatgpt.site/blog/specifying-security-screw-drive/
Last modified: 2026-10-29

DESIGN & DIMENSIONS / 2 MIN READ

### How to specify a tamper-resistant screw drive

A security-drive name is a starting point, not a complete interface specification. The recess, matching tool and available assembly access must work together.

By Theo Wan • ZUFEK Technical Editorial • Published October 29, 2026 Multi-Station Cold Heading

IN THIS GUIDE Identify the exact interface Define the head and tool access Review pin and recess features Separate access resistance from joint performance RELATED PRODUCT Security & Tamper-Resistant Screws ↗

#### Identify the exact interface

Pin-in six-lobe, five-lobe, Y-type, triangle and two-hole spanner designs are different interfaces. Even visually similar recesses can have incompatible profiles. Supply a controlled drive drawing, recognized interface reference or approved matching tool rather than asking a manufacturer to copy a small photograph.

#### Define the head and tool access

Head diameter, height and surrounding enclosure affect whether the intended tool can reach the recess. Show the assembled condition, including any counterbore or nearby wall. A usable loose screw can become difficult to service after it is installed inside the product.

Working on this type of part? Explore our security & tamper-resistant screws and include the functional requirements in your RFQ.

#### Review pin and recess features

For a center-pin drive, include the pin geometry, recess depth and relevant edge condition. Forming and secondary machining offer different ways to create these details. Inspect the functional tool engagement as well as the external head dimensions; a recess can look correct while fitting poorly.

#### Separate access resistance from joint performance

A special drive can discourage casual removal, but it does not make a joint impossible to open. Material, thread engagement and the tightening method still determine the mechanical connection. Define service access, installation torque requirements and the intended tool-control arrangement independently.

#### Specification example

For an enclosure fastener, supply the enclosure recess and service-tool outline alongside the screw drawing. This allows the quotation review to consider drive engagement and access together before tooling is selected.

#### RFQ checklist

Drive drawing or approved tool

Head envelope and access clearance

Pin and recess dimensions

Material, finish and quantity

Functional tool-fit acceptance

### Hollow screw bores: the details an RFQ should include
Source: https://precision-custom-fasteners-yang.boldshrew261.chatgpt.site/blog/hollow-screw-bore-specification/
Last modified: 2026-10-29

DESIGN & DIMENSIONS / 2 MIN READ

### Hollow screw bores: the details an RFQ should include

An axial hole changes both manufacturing and inspection. A useful hollow-screw specification explains the passage, the surrounding wall and the conditions inside the bore.

By Theo Wan • ZUFEK Technical Editorial • Published October 29, 2026 Swiss-Type & CNC Turning

IN THIS GUIDE Describe the entire passage Review wall thickness with the thread State edge and cleanliness requirements Define functional tests separately RELATED PRODUCT Hollow & Through-Hole Screws ↗

#### Describe the entire passage

Identify whether the hole is through, blind, stepped or connected to a side passage. Dimension each section and its axial position. A single opening diameter does not define an internal path, and a photograph cannot establish hidden counterbores or restrictions.

#### Review wall thickness with the thread

The bore and external thread share the same material section. Show their relationship through the thinnest region and identify any concentricity or position requirement. Manufacturing review needs the actual geometry; an outside diameter alone is not sufficient to evaluate a hollow threaded feature.

Working on this type of part? Explore our hollow & through-hole screws and include the functional requirements in your RFQ.

#### State edge and cleanliness requirements

Drilling can leave burrs at hole exits and intersections. Specify which edges must be broken and how internal burrs will be accepted. If the part carries fluid, adhesive or a wire, explain the relevant contamination, surface-damage or blockage concern rather than relying on a generic clean note.

#### Define functional tests separately

A continuous bore does not itself prove pressure capability, leak tightness or unrestricted flow in an assembly. State any test medium, fixture arrangement and acceptance method that the application requires. These conditions should be agreed before sampling so manufacturing and inspection can be quoted together.

#### Specification example

For a screw used as a cable passage, show the cable envelope and the edges it contacts. For a fluid passage, describe the intended sealing interface separately from the through hole.

#### RFQ checklist

Complete bore section

Minimum wall and feature relationship

Hole exit and intersection burr limits

Internal cleanliness requirements

Required functional test method

### Designing the bearing face of a custom flange screw
Source: https://precision-custom-fasteners-yang.boldshrew261.chatgpt.site/blog/custom-flange-bearing-face/
Last modified: 2026-10-29

DESIGN & DIMENSIONS / 2 MIN READ

### Designing the bearing face of a custom flange screw

A flange is more than a larger circle under the head. Its bearing face, stiffness and clearance must match the component being clamped.

By Theo Wan • ZUFEK Technical Editorial • Published October 29, 2026 Multi-Station Cold Heading

IN THIS GUIDE Start with the mating surface Dimension the flange as a functional feature Choose the face condition deliberately Include the finish and tightening conditions RELATED PRODUCT Custom Flange Screws ↗

#### Start with the mating surface

Identify the material beneath the flange and the available contact area. A soft panel, coated bracket and rigid machined seat respond differently. Show holes, slots and nearby edges so the bearing footprint can be reviewed against the real supporting surface.

#### Dimension the flange as a functional feature

Specify diameter, thickness and the transition beneath the head. Include flatness or surface requirements when they affect contact. Thin flanges and large overhangs should not be assumed to distribute load uniformly; their behavior needs review with the intended connection and material condition.

Working on this type of part? Explore our custom flange screws and include the functional requirements in your RFQ.

#### Choose the face condition deliberately

Plain, textured and serrated bearing faces are not interchangeable. A serration may change the contact behavior and affect a coating or soft surface. Explain whether the priority is appearance, resistance to movement, contact pressure or another function, then agree the relevant acceptance checks.

#### Include the finish and tightening conditions

Coating thickness and friction can influence the assembled joint. Treat the flange face and threads as specified surfaces, not simply parts of an overall color requirement. Any comparison with a washer assembly should consider the complete joint rather than the number of handled components.

#### Specification example

When replacing a loose washer with an integral flange, provide both assembly drawings. The review should compare the supporting footprint and seating condition before treating the two arrangements as equivalent.

#### RFQ checklist

Mating material and hole shape

Flange diameter and thickness

Bearing-face condition

Clearance and finish requirements

Assembly acceptance criteria

### Knurled thumb screws: specifying grip and adjustment
Source: https://precision-custom-fasteners-yang.boldshrew261.chatgpt.site/blog/knurled-thumb-screw-grip-design/
Last modified: 2026-10-29

DESIGN & DIMENSIONS / 2 MIN READ

### Knurled thumb screws: specifying grip and adjustment

A hand-adjusted screw must be accessible, comfortable to grip and compatible with the required adjustment. Head texture alone does not define how the mechanism works.

By Theo Wan • ZUFEK Technical Editorial • Published October 29, 2026 Swiss-Type & CNC Turning

IN THIS GUIDE Describe the way it is operated Specify the knurl rather than an appearance Connect pitch to the adjustment requirement Decide whether a service drive is needed RELATED PRODUCT Knurled Thumb & Adjustment Screws ↗

#### Describe the way it is operated

Explain whether the user adjusts the part frequently, wears gloves or works in a restricted space. Head diameter and height influence access as much as the knurl pattern. Include surrounding components so the manufacturer can review usable grip clearance rather than only the isolated head.

#### Specify the knurl rather than an appearance

Straight and diamond patterns provide different textures. State the required head envelope and any controlled pattern details. Agree acceptable surface and edge condition, especially where users handle the component repeatedly. A reference sample can support the discussion, but the approved requirements should be recorded.

Working on this type of part? Explore our knurled thumb & adjustment screws and include the functional requirements in your RFQ.

#### Connect pitch to the adjustment requirement

Describe the required travel, mating thread and any backlash or position-holding concern. Fine pitch may provide smaller movement per turn, but the complete mechanism determines useful adjustment. Specify a separate locking feature if the setting must remain stable under service conditions.

#### Decide whether a service drive is needed

A slot or socket may supplement hand operation, but it can introduce a different tightening method. Clarify how each interface is intended to be used. Do not assume a hand-grip feature establishes a controlled tightening torque or prevents the operator from overloading the assembly.

#### Specification example

For an adjustable fixture stop, include the usable adjustment range and the contact surface at the tip. This helps separate grip design from the positioning and locking functions.

#### RFQ checklist

Available finger and tool clearance

Head dimensions and knurl pattern

Adjustment travel and mating thread

Locking or retention arrangement

Surface and edge acceptance

### Cone, flat, dog or cup: choosing a set-screw tip
Source: https://precision-custom-fasteners-yang.boldshrew261.chatgpt.site/blog/set-screw-tip-selection/
Last modified: 2026-10-29

DESIGN & DIMENSIONS / 2 MIN READ

### Cone, flat, dog or cup: choosing a set-screw tip

The end of a set screw defines how it contacts the mating component. Choose the tip around the required contact and permitted surface change, not only the screw diameter.

By Theo Wan • ZUFEK Technical Editorial • Published October 29, 2026 Swiss-Type & CNC Turning

IN THIS GUIDE Identify what the tip contacts Compare the actual end geometries Review marking and repeated adjustment Define engagement and acceptance RELATED PRODUCT Custom Set Screws & Grub Screws ↗

#### Identify what the tip contacts

Show the shaft, flat, groove or hole beneath the screw. A tip contacting a curved surface behaves differently from one engaging a prepared recess. Explain whether the connection is intended to clamp, locate, stop travel or provide an anti-rotation feature.

#### Compare the actual end geometries

Cone, flat, cylindrical dog and cup points are different contact forms. Dimension the functional features of the selected end and its relationship to the thread. Avoid treating a generic tip name as permission for any manufacturer-specific interpretation of the shape.

Working on this type of part? Explore our custom set screws & grub screws and include the functional requirements in your RFQ.

#### Review marking and repeated adjustment

State whether the mating surface may be indented or scratched and whether the screw will be repositioned. Surface condition can become important when a setting is changed repeatedly. Tip material condition, finish and the mating material should be reviewed as part of the same contact system.

#### Define engagement and acceptance

Thread engagement, drive access and installation requirements still matter on a headless part. Agree a dimensional check for the tip and any assembly test needed for the intended function. A correct tip outline alone does not establish a holding-force or torque rating.

#### Specification example

If a dog point enters a prepared hole, supply that hole geometry with the screw drawing. The cylindrical extension and the mating hole should be reviewed together rather than specified independently.

#### RFQ checklist

Mating surface or recess

Tip form and controlled dimensions

Allowed surface marking

Thread engagement and drive

Functional acceptance requirement

### T-slot bolt fit: what to measure before ordering
Source: https://precision-custom-fasteners-yang.boldshrew261.chatgpt.site/blog/t-slot-bolt-head-fit/
Last modified: 2026-10-29

DESIGN & DIMENSIONS / 2 MIN READ

### T-slot bolt fit: what to measure before ordering

A T-head must enter, turn or slide inside the intended slot while retaining the required contact. The slot cross-section is therefore an essential part of the fastener RFQ.

By Theo Wan • ZUFEK Technical Editorial • Published October 29, 2026 Multi-Station Cold Heading

IN THIS GUIDE Provide the complete slot section Explain the insertion method Review contact and anti-rotation Check the finished condition RELATED PRODUCT Custom T-Slot Bolts ↗

#### Provide the complete slot section

Measure the opening, internal width, depth and any corner radii. Explain which dimensions are controlled and whether the profile varies along the assembly. A nominal extrusion family or a top-view photograph may leave important internal clearances undefined.

#### Explain the insertion method

Some heads enter from a slot end; others must pass through the opening and rotate. These are different geometric requirements. Show the intended assembly sequence and any end stops or surrounding parts that prevent the movement assumed during installation.

Working on this type of part? Explore our custom t-slot bolts and include the functional requirements in your RFQ.

#### Review contact and anti-rotation

Head thickness, bearing faces and neck geometry influence how the bolt seats in the slot. Specify the required clearances and contact surfaces. A head that can be inserted is not automatically suitable for the required clamping load or resistance to rotation.

#### Check the finished condition

Coating and edge finishing can alter the available clearance. Agree the final head envelope and inspect the relevant features after finishing. A trial fit in an approved mating section may be useful, but it should support clearly documented dimensional and functional requirements.

#### Specification example

For a bolt that must rotate inside an aluminum profile, provide the rotation envelope as well as the installed position. This identifies interference that a single assembled view may hide.

#### RFQ checklist

Slot cross-section and radii

Insertion and rotation sequence

Head and neck clearances

Finished coating allowance

Agreed fit and clamping checks

### Eye bolts for linkages and lifting: different specification needs
Source: https://precision-custom-fasteners-yang.boldshrew261.chatgpt.site/blog/eye-bolt-linkage-vs-lifting/
Last modified: 2026-10-29

DESIGN & DIMENSIONS / 2 MIN READ

### Eye bolts for linkages and lifting: different specification needs

An eye-shaped end can belong to a linkage, a tensioning device or a lifting component. Similar appearance does not establish the same design requirements or approved use.

By Theo Wan • ZUFEK Technical Editorial • Published October 29, 2026 Hot Heading & Forging

IN THIS GUIDE Define the intended function first Show the articulation and load direction Treat lifting requirements explicitly Prepare a complete manufacturing review RELATED PRODUCT Custom Eye & Articulating Bolts ↗

#### Define the intended function first

State how the component connects and how force enters the eye. Include the pin, supporting parts and expected movement. A flat drilled lug, a fork and a closed forged ring create different interfaces even when each is casually called an eye bolt.

#### Show the articulation and load direction

Provide the range of movement and surrounding clearances. Identify whether the connection sees aligned tension, angular loading or changing directions. These details help the responsible engineer assess the load path and select the dimensions that require control.

Working on this type of part? Explore our custom eye & articulating bolts and include the functional requirements in your RFQ.

#### Treat lifting requirements explicitly

A custom ring geometry is not a working-load rating. Lifting-related use requires an approved design basis, suitable material condition and the specified verification and documentation. Do not infer a rating from dimensions, appearance or similarity to an unrelated catalog component.

#### Prepare a complete manufacturing review

Dimension the eye, shank transitions, thread and seating faces. State the required properties and acceptance checks. The forming and machining sequence should be considered with the function, rather than selecting a production method before the application requirements are understood.

#### Specification example

For a pivoting fixture connection, provide the mating clevis and pin. For a lifting requirement, include the approved lifting specification instead of using the fixture drawing as a substitute.

#### RFQ checklist

Linkage or lifting use

Mating pin and movement envelope

Load directions and design requirements

Material and final condition

Required verification and records

### How to dimension a custom U-bolt
Source: https://precision-custom-fasteners-yang.boldshrew261.chatgpt.site/blog/u-bolt-bend-and-leg-dimensions/
Last modified: 2026-10-29

DESIGN & DIMENSIONS / 2 MIN READ

### How to dimension a custom U-bolt

Inside width, bend shape and leg alignment determine whether a U-bolt fits the supported component. A clear drawing separates those features from the threaded connection.

By Theo Wan • ZUFEK Technical Editorial • Published October 29, 2026 Secondary & Precision Operations

IN THIS GUIDE Identify the component being clamped Dimension from consistent references Review bending and the material condition Include the rest of the joint RELATED PRODUCT Custom U-Bolts ↗

#### Identify the component being clamped

Provide the pipe or frame cross-section and any saddle or liner. State whether contact is intended along a radius or against flat faces. The nominal outside size may not describe corner radii, coatings or protective layers that affect the actual fit.

#### Dimension from consistent references

Show inside width, bend radius or profile, leg length and threaded length using clear references. Avoid mixing outside and inside dimensions without defining the rod section. Include leg parallelism or position requirements when they affect installation into a bracket or plate.

Working on this type of part? Explore our custom u-bolts and include the functional requirements in your RFQ.

#### Review bending and the material condition

The selected grade, section and final condition affect how the bend is produced and verified. Specify mechanical and surface requirements instead of assuming any rod can be bent to the same shape without consequences. Manufacturing feasibility must be confirmed for the actual geometry.

#### Include the rest of the joint

Nuts, washers, saddles and supporting plates form the complete connection. Identify required engagement and any assembly restrictions. Agree the finished coating and a useful fit check so production inspection evaluates the part in the condition that will be supplied.

#### Specification example

If the U-bolt passes through two holes in a plate, supply the hole spacing and clearance. A correct bend profile alone does not guarantee that both threaded legs will enter the plate.

#### RFQ checklist

Clamped cross-section and liner

Inside width and bend profile

Leg length and alignment

Threaded engagement

Material, finish and fit check

### Custom carriage bolts: specifying the square neck
Source: https://precision-custom-fasteners-yang.boldshrew261.chatgpt.site/blog/carriage-bolt-square-neck/
Last modified: 2026-10-29

DESIGN & DIMENSIONS / 2 MIN READ

### Custom carriage bolts: specifying the square neck

The square neck is the functional anti-rotation feature of a carriage bolt. It should be matched to the mating hole and supporting material rather than treated as a cosmetic detail.

By Theo Wan • ZUFEK Technical Editorial • Published October 29, 2026 Multi-Station Cold Heading

IN THIS GUIDE Define the mating hole Control neck depth and transition Review the domed head and bearing face Agree the finished fit RELATED PRODUCT Custom Carriage Bolts ↗

#### Define the mating hole

Provide hole shape, dimensions, corner condition and panel thickness. Explain whether the neck is intended to enter freely or engage during installation. The behavior depends on both the neck and the surrounding material, not simply the width across flats.

#### Control neck depth and transition

Specify square-neck length and its relationship to the head underside. Show transitions that affect seating in the panel. A neck that is too long for the stack can interfere with the nut-side assembly even when the head and thread dimensions are correct.

Working on this type of part? Explore our custom carriage bolts and include the functional requirements in your RFQ.

#### Review the domed head and bearing face

Head diameter and height affect appearance, clearance and the supporting footprint. Identify visible surfaces and any finish requirements. A smooth dome does not define the underside contact, so include the seating details that matter to the connection.

#### Agree the finished fit

Forming variation, coating and hole condition can influence assembly. Inspect the neck in the supplied finish and define any functional fit or anti-rotation check. Do not use a visual comparison with a standard carriage bolt as the only acceptance method for a custom neck.

#### Specification example

When adapting a carriage bolt to a thinner panel, review neck depth and the full clamp stack. Changing only the thread length may leave the actual seating problem unresolved.

#### RFQ checklist

Mating square hole and panel thickness

Neck width and depth

Under-head transitions

Finished head envelope

Fit and anti-rotation acceptance

### Eccentric screw drawings: making the offset unambiguous
Source: https://precision-custom-fasteners-yang.boldshrew261.chatgpt.site/blog/eccentric-screw-datum-drawing/
Last modified: 2026-10-29

DESIGN & DIMENSIONS / 2 MIN READ

### Eccentric screw drawings: making the offset unambiguous

An eccentric feature needs a clear reference axis. Without a datum scheme, two manufacturers can interpret an apparently simple offset drawing differently.

By Theo Wan • ZUFEK Technical Editorial • Published October 29, 2026 Swiss-Type & CNC Turning

IN THIS GUIDE Identify the functional axis Define offset and angular orientation Describe the mating contact Choose an inspection setup that follows function RELATED PRODUCT Eccentric & Angled Head Screws ↗

#### Identify the functional axis

Show which shank, shoulder or thread establishes the assembly reference. Dimension the eccentric feature relative to that reference rather than an arbitrary drawing edge. If the thread does not locate the part in service, explain which smooth feature actually does.

#### Define offset and angular orientation

Specify the amount of eccentricity and any required orientation to a slot, flat or drive. An offset without angular control may be acceptable for one adjuster and unsuitable for another. Include the intended adjustment positions and how they will be identified during assembly.

Working on this type of part? Explore our eccentric & angled head screws and include the functional requirements in your RFQ.

#### Describe the mating contact

Provide the follower, bore or surface moved by the eccentric feature. Show clearances and travel limits. The assembly determines whether a geometric change produces the desired adjustment; the screw drawing alone cannot establish the motion of every connected component.

#### Choose an inspection setup that follows function

The inspection plan should establish the same reference features used in the design. Discuss the practical measurement of offset, form and orientation before production. A photograph can illustrate the concept but is not an adequate substitute for controlled datum and dimensional requirements.

#### Specification example

For a camera-module adjuster, show the feature that contacts the module and the surface that locates the screw. This helps distinguish the adjustment geometry from incidental machining surfaces.

#### RFQ checklist

Functional locating axis

Offset and orientation

Mating contact and travel

Critical datum relationships

Agreed measurement setup

### Double-ended studs: preventing mixed-thread assembly errors
Source: https://precision-custom-fasteners-yang.boldshrew261.chatgpt.site/blog/double-ended-stud-thread-identification/
Last modified: 2026-10-29

DESIGN & DIMENSIONS / 2 MIN READ

### Double-ended studs: preventing mixed-thread assembly errors

Different threads at the two ends can solve an interface problem and create an identification problem. The drawing, inspection plan and packaging should distinguish each end clearly.

By Theo Wan • ZUFEK Technical Editorial • Published October 29, 2026 Swiss-Type & CNC Turning

IN THIS GUIDE Specify the two ends independently Explain the center section Plan identification before packing Gauge and review both interfaces RELATED PRODUCT Custom Double-Ended Studs ↗

#### Specify the two ends independently

Provide diameter, pitch, handedness, fit and usable length for each threaded end. Do not assume a repeated note applies to both ends if the interfaces differ. Show any thread runout or relief that affects seating against the center section.

#### Explain the center section

A plain shank, shoulder or wrench flat can serve a locating or assembly function. Dimension its axial relationship to both threads. Clarify whether a face should seat against a mating part or whether the stud is installed to a separate depth requirement.

Working on this type of part? Explore our custom double-ended studs and include the functional requirements in your RFQ.

#### Plan identification before packing

If the ends look similar, discuss permitted marks, packaging orientation or another agreed distinction. Avoid an unapproved color or permanent mark on a functional surface. Identification requirements should appear in the order documentation so repeat batches use the same method.

#### Gauge and review both interfaces

Each end needs the appropriate acceptance method for its own specification. Inspection records should identify the end being checked, especially when the same nominal diameter uses different pitches. A successful trial in one mating part does not establish the other end conforms.

#### Specification example

For a stud joining two different thread sizes, label the ends A and B on the drawing and use the same labels in the inspection plan. Keep that convention on sample reports and packaging instructions.

#### RFQ checklist

Complete specification for both threads

Center-section dimensions

Installation sequence and seating

Approved end identification

Separate thread acceptance checks

### Reduced-shank screws: why transitions need attention
Source: https://precision-custom-fasteners-yang.boldshrew261.chatgpt.site/blog/reduced-shank-transition-design/
Last modified: 2026-10-29

DESIGN & DIMENSIONS / 2 MIN READ

### Reduced-shank screws: why transitions need attention

A narrow center section changes the geometry of a threaded connection. Its purpose and transition details must be defined before the manufacturing route is selected.

By Theo Wan • ZUFEK Technical Editorial • Published October 29, 2026 Swiss-Type & CNC Turning

IN THIS GUIDE State the purpose of the reduced section Dimension the whole transition Review properties with the responsible engineer Inspect the supplied condition RELATED PRODUCT Reduced & Variable Shank Screws ↗

#### State the purpose of the reduced section

Explain whether the waist provides clearance, a specified compliance characteristic or another design function. These are different requirements. A visually similar reduction can perform differently when the section length, material condition or surrounding joint changes.

#### Dimension the whole transition

Include the minimum diameter, axial length and transition radii or reliefs. Identify functional surfaces and features that may be blended. Leaving a transition to general workshop practice can create variation where the designer expected a consistent section and load path.

Working on this type of part? Explore our reduced & variable shank screws and include the functional requirements in your RFQ.

#### Review properties with the responsible engineer

A reduced shank is not automatically a remedy for cracking or fatigue. Required mechanical behavior depends on the complete joint and loading. Supply the relevant design requirements and agree any testing rather than treating the geometry as a universal performance improvement.

#### Inspect the supplied condition

Heat treatment, finishing and local machining marks may matter at a transition. Define the required surface condition and final dimensional checks. When several production routes are possible, compare them against the functional requirements instead of accepting a route solely because it has a familiar name.

#### Specification example

For a clearance-driven design, provide the interfering component envelope. If the reduced section has a mechanical function, include the approved engineering requirements separately from the clearance drawing.

#### RFQ checklist

Functional reason for the waist

Minimum diameter and length

Transition radii and surface condition

Material and final properties

Required verification

### Tapered screws: defining the mating seat
Source: https://precision-custom-fasteners-yang.boldshrew261.chatgpt.site/blog/tapered-screw-mating-seat/
Last modified: 2026-10-29

DESIGN & DIMENSIONS / 2 MIN READ

### Tapered screws: defining the mating seat

A taper works against a corresponding surface. Its angle, axial position and relationship to the thread must be considered with the mating component.

By Theo Wan • ZUFEK Technical Editorial • Published October 29, 2026 Swiss-Type & CNC Turning

IN THIS GUIDE Describe what the taper is meant to do Use a complete dimensional definition Relate the taper to the thread and datums Agree a useful verification method RELATED PRODUCT Tapered Shank & Cone Screws ↗

#### Describe what the taper is meant to do

Centering, contact and sealing are distinct functions. Identify the intended contact surface and the motion or loading involved. A conical shape does not itself demonstrate sealing performance or establish the location of a connected assembly.

#### Use a complete dimensional definition

Specify angle or taper ratio with the necessary diameters and axial references. Make it clear where the taper begins and ends. Avoid redundant or conflicting dimensions that imply different surfaces when interpreted at the manufacturing or inspection stage.

Working on this type of part? Explore our tapered shank & cone screws and include the functional requirements in your RFQ.

#### Relate the taper to the thread and datums

Show the reference axis, seating location and usable thread engagement. If the taper establishes location, say so. The required relationship between the cone and other features should follow the assembly function rather than an assumption that every surface must share the tightest tolerance.

#### Agree a useful verification method

Discuss dimensional and contact checks against an approved mating reference where appropriate. If sealing is required, define a separate functional test with its own conditions and acceptance criteria. Checking a cone angle alone does not prove the completed assembly will seal.

#### Specification example

For a locating cone, provide the corresponding seat and insertion limit. For a sealing design, also provide the sealing arrangement and required test rather than relying on a generic taper note.

#### RFQ checklist

Intended locating or sealing function

Taper definition and axial position

Mating seat drawing

Datum and thread relationship

Dimensional and functional checks

Ready to discuss your part? Use the RFQ preparation checklist , then submit your drawing for review . For acceptance requirements, see quality planning .

General guidance only. Material properties, tolerances, standards and manufacturing feasibility must be verified for the actual specification. This article does not establish a product performance guarantee.

### Integral locating pins: coordinating pin and screw datums
Source: https://precision-custom-fasteners-yang.boldshrew261.chatgpt.site/blog/integral-locating-pin-position/
Last modified: 2026-10-29

DESIGN & DIMENSIONS / 2 MIN READ

### Integral locating pins: coordinating pin and screw datums

Combining a small locating pin with a screw can reduce separate components, but the locating and clamping functions still need distinct specifications.

By Theo Wan • ZUFEK Technical Editorial • Published October 29, 2026 Swiss-Type & CNC Turning

IN THIS GUIDE Identify which feature locates Define the pin position and orientation Review the installation sequence Check the complete functional geometry RELATED PRODUCT Screws with Integral Locating Pins ↗

#### Identify which feature locates

Explain whether the pin establishes lateral position while the screw supplies clamp load, or whether another feature controls the assembly. Include the mating hole and seating surface. Without that information, a manufacturer cannot tell which relationships are functionally critical.

#### Define the pin position and orientation

Specify pin diameter, projection and position relative to the selected reference features. An offset pin may also need angular orientation to the head or drive. Use a clear datum scheme so machining and inspection establish the same relationship.

Working on this type of part? Explore our screws with integral locating pins and include the functional requirements in your RFQ.

#### Review the installation sequence

Show how the pin enters its hole before or during thread engagement. Consider surrounding clearance and any movement available in the mating components. A single component can be dimensionally correct but difficult to install if the assembly sequence was not considered.

#### Check the complete functional geometry

Inspect pin dimensions, position and relevant seating faces. If a functional assembly check is used, document the mating reference and acceptance method. Do not rely on the appearance of the pin or successful thread engagement as proof that the locating requirement is satisfied.

#### Specification example

For a screw with a pin under its flange, provide the hole pattern and the flange seating face. These details allow the pin location to be evaluated in the same assembly condition in which it will operate.

#### RFQ checklist

Locating versus clamping function

Pin diameter and projection

Position and angular datums

Mating hole and assembly sequence

Functional acceptance reference

### Multi-step screws: controlling the axial dimension chain
Source: https://precision-custom-fasteners-yang.boldshrew261.chatgpt.site/blog/multi-step-screw-dimension-chain/
Last modified: 2026-10-29

DESIGN & DIMENSIONS / 2 MIN READ

### Multi-step screws: controlling the axial dimension chain

Several shoulders can locate several components. A clear dimension scheme explains which axial distances control the assembly and which are consequences of other dimensions.

By Theo Wan • ZUFEK Technical Editorial • Published October 29, 2026 Cold Heading + Secondary Machining

IN THIS GUIDE Map the shoulder to each mating component Choose a consistent reference scheme Review transitions and tool access Inspect the relevant relationships RELATED PRODUCT Multi-Step & Multi-Shoulder Screws ↗

#### Map the shoulder to each mating component

Identify which face supports each component in the stack. Include the mating parts or a simplified section showing their position. This helps separate functional locating shoulders from machining transitions that do not establish an assembly position.

#### Choose a consistent reference scheme

Baseline dimensions and chained dimensions communicate different relationships. The responsible designer should select the scheme that matches the required function and tolerance analysis. Avoid adding a closed chain of conflicting controlled dimensions simply to fill every gap on the drawing.

Working on this type of part? Explore our multi-step & multi-shoulder screws and include the functional requirements in your RFQ.

#### Review transitions and tool access

Small reliefs, corner radii and edge breaks can affect how a component seats against a shoulder. Show the mating corner conditions and identify features that must remain clear. Secondary machining or finishing needs to preserve the approved seating geometry.

#### Inspect the relevant relationships

A collection of individual lengths does not always establish the functional stack. Agree measurement references and checks for the distances that matter. Include final coating and treatment conditions when they can affect the supplied diameters or seating surfaces.

#### Specification example

For two bearings separated by a shoulder, identify the bearing seating faces and the required spacing between them. This is more useful than applying the same tight tolerance to every unrelated axial dimension.

#### RFQ checklist

Mating stack or section view

Functional locating shoulders

Datum-based axial dimensions

Corner and relief requirements

Final-condition inspection references

### Custom clinch studs: specify the panel as well as the fastener
Source: https://precision-custom-fasteners-yang.boldshrew261.chatgpt.site/blog/clinch-stud-panel-requirements/
Last modified: 2026-10-29

DESIGN & DIMENSIONS / 2 MIN READ

### Custom clinch studs: specify the panel as well as the fastener

A press-in connection depends on the panel, hole and installation process. A custom stud cannot be evaluated as an isolated threaded shape.

By Theo Wan • ZUFEK Technical Editorial • Published October 29, 2026 Multi-Station Cold Heading

IN THIS GUIDE Provide the panel condition Define the hole and retention geometry Review tooling support and installation Specify acceptance beyond appearance RELATED PRODUCT Custom Clinch Screws & Studs ↗

#### Provide the panel condition

Specify panel material, thickness, hardness where required and any finish present during installation. Include local geometry and access for the press tooling. These conditions influence how the sheet engages the retention features and how the finished connection can be verified.

#### Define the hole and retention geometry

Show hole dimensions, preparation and permitted edge condition. Define the stud undercut, serrations or other press-in features on the approved drawing. A resemblance to a standard proprietary part does not establish that the custom version has the same installation requirements or ratings.

Working on this type of part? Explore our custom clinch screws & studs and include the functional requirements in your RFQ.

#### Review tooling support and installation

Explain how the panel and stud will be supported during pressing. Avoid applying an installation condition copied from a different component without review. Agree sample assembly requirements so the proposed fastener and the actual panel can be evaluated together.

#### Specify acceptance beyond appearance

Where relevant, define push-out, torque-out or other functional checks with methods and criteria. A flush-looking head does not by itself prove retention. The quotation should distinguish dimensional inspection of the stud from qualification of the pressed panel assembly.

#### Specification example

For a custom stud in a coated panel, state whether coating occurs before or after installation. That sequence can change the fit and the inspection conditions and should be resolved before production.

#### RFQ checklist

Panel material and thickness

Hole preparation and dimensions

Stud retention features

Press support and sample assembly

Functional retention tests

### Rolled or cut threads: questions to resolve in the RFQ
Source: https://precision-custom-fasteners-yang.boldshrew261.chatgpt.site/blog/rolled-vs-cut-thread-rfq/
Last modified: 2026-10-29

MANUFACTURING / 2 MIN READ

### Rolled or cut threads: questions to resolve in the RFQ

Thread generation is a process choice, while thread geometry and acceptance are product requirements. A complete RFQ explains both without confusing the method with a guaranteed result.

By Theo Wan • ZUFEK Technical Editorial • Published October 29, 2026 Thread Rolling, Cutting & Tapping

IN THIS GUIDE Define the thread before the production method Review material and the proposed sequence Avoid a universal strength ranking Agree the finished acceptance method RELATED PRODUCT Special & Compound Thread Profiles ↗

#### Define the thread before the production method

Provide designation, profile, pitch, tolerance class and usable engagement. Include special roots, crests or transitions where applicable. A request to roll the thread does not resolve an incomplete thread specification, and a generic thread name may not define a custom profile.

#### Review material and the proposed sequence

Rolling displaces material; cutting removes material. Their feasibility depends on the grade, condition, geometry and available tooling. Discuss the sequence relative to heat treatment and other finishing operations rather than assuming the same process can be transferred unchanged to a different material.

Working on this type of part? Explore our special & compound thread profiles and include the functional requirements in your RFQ.

#### Avoid a universal strength ranking

Rolling may provide useful surface and material effects in suitable conditions, but the finished connection still needs the specified properties and acceptance. Cutting can be appropriate for many special geometries and quantities. Process labels alone should not replace the design or verification of the actual component.

#### Agree the finished acceptance method

State the required gauging, dimensional checks and any profile verification. Inspection should evaluate the final supplied condition, including coating where relevant. If a manufacturing method is mandatory, record it explicitly and explain any approval requirement for a proposed route change.

#### Specification example

For a short run of a special trapezoidal thread, provide the complete profile and mating requirement. Ask the supplier to explain the proposed route instead of selecting a process solely from a general cost comparison.

#### RFQ checklist

Complete thread geometry

Material and final condition

Treatment and threading sequence

Mandatory versus preferred method

Final thread acceptance

### Cross holes in screws: planning burr control and inspection
Source: https://precision-custom-fasteners-yang.boldshrew261.chatgpt.site/blog/cross-hole-burr-control/
Last modified: 2026-10-29

MANUFACTURING / 2 MIN READ

### Cross holes in screws: planning burr control and inspection

A drilled cross hole creates entry and exit edges, and may intersect another feature. The RFQ should define those edges as carefully as the hole location.

By Theo Wan • ZUFEK Technical Editorial • Published October 29, 2026 Secondary & Precision Operations

IN THIS GUIDE Show every intersection Specify edge condition rather than a vague note Review the process with the feature access Make the inspection practical RELATED PRODUCT Cross-Drilled & Head-Hole Screws ↗

#### Show every intersection

Include sections where the hole crosses a bore, groove or thread. State the functional purpose of the passage and which surfaces the pin, wire or fluid contacts. An external view may hide the most difficult burr-removal location inside the component.

#### Specify edge condition rather than a vague note

An instruction to remove burrs needs an acceptance basis. Identify permitted edge breaks and surfaces that must retain their geometry. Excessive edge removal can change a small locating feature, while an inaccessible residual burr can interfere with the assembly or passage.

Working on this type of part? Explore our cross-drilled & head-hole screws and include the functional requirements in your RFQ.

#### Review the process with the feature access

Drilling order, fixturing and subsequent finishing influence access to the edges. Agree how the proposed route handles the exit and any internal intersection. A later cleaning operation removes loose contamination but should not be assumed to eliminate attached machining burrs.

#### Make the inspection practical

Define where visual, optical or other checks are needed and how the difficult area will be evaluated. A pin-fit test may check one function without proving all edges meet the required condition. Keep the dimensional, functional and cleanliness requirements distinct in the inspection plan.

#### Specification example

For a transverse pin hole through a hollow screw, show the internal intersection and describe how the pin is inserted. This gives the manufacturer a concrete edge condition to review before quoting.

#### RFQ checklist

Hole position and direction

Internal intersections

Permitted edge breaks

Deburring access and sequence

Agreed inspection method

### Coating allowance for threads and precision shoulders
Source: https://precision-custom-fasteners-yang.boldshrew261.chatgpt.site/blog/coating-allowance-thread-shoulder/
Last modified: 2026-10-29

MATERIALS & FINISHES / 2 MIN READ

### Coating allowance for threads and precision shoulders

A coating belongs in the dimensional plan. The final fit must be evaluated in the condition that the customer receives, not only before surface treatment.

By Theo Wan • ZUFEK Technical Editorial • Published October 29, 2026 Secondary & Precision Operations

IN THIS GUIDE Identify the surfaces that control fit Specify the actual coating system Resolve the inspection stage Include local finish restrictions RELATED PRODUCT Shoulder & Step Screws ↗

#### Identify the surfaces that control fit

Mark the shoulder, thread, bearing face and any bore that interfaces with another component. Explain whether coating is required, permitted or excluded on each functional area. An all-over finish note may conflict with a fit that the drawing defines without considering the surface system.

#### Specify the actual coating system

Name the relevant finish requirement and thickness controls rather than using color alone. Different systems can have different dimensional and friction effects. The manufacturer needs the agreed system to propose appropriate preparation and finishing allowances for the specific geometry.

Working on this type of part? Explore our shoulder & step screws and include the functional requirements in your RFQ.

#### Resolve the inspection stage

State whether dimensions refer to the pre-coating or final condition. If both stages matter, identify their separate limits and checks. Do not assume that a shoulder accepted before finishing or a thread accepted before coating will automatically meet the final assembly requirement.

#### Include local finish restrictions

Masking, selective treatment or post-finish operations may be relevant, but must be reviewed for feasibility and function. Agree any permitted bare surfaces and protection requirements. A route change intended to rescue a fit should not silently change the approved surface condition.

#### Specification example

For a locating shoulder with a coated thread, distinguish the two surface requirements on the drawing. This allows the manufacturer to review whether one uniform treatment is appropriate.

#### RFQ checklist

Functional coated surfaces

Finish system and thickness requirements

Pre-finish versus final dimensions

Selective coating restrictions

Final thread and shoulder checks

### Nickel plating and stainless passivation: different RFQ requirements
Source: https://precision-custom-fasteners-yang.boldshrew261.chatgpt.site/blog/nickel-plating-vs-stainless-passivation/
Last modified: 2026-10-29

MATERIALS & FINISHES / 2 MIN READ

### Nickel plating and stainless passivation: different RFQ requirements

A bright appearance does not identify a surface process. Specify the substrate and required surface function before choosing between plating, passivation or another treatment.

By Theo Wan • ZUFEK Technical Editorial • Published October 29, 2026 Coatings & Surface Treatments

IN THIS GUIDE Begin with the material underneath Distinguish the process purpose Consider dimensional and assembly effects Agree evidence and acceptance RELATED PRODUCT Custom Metal Screws ↗

#### Begin with the material underneath

State the exact base material and condition. A finish suitable for one substrate may be inappropriate for another. Do not use a photograph of a shiny screw as evidence that the same treatment can be applied to a different grade or component without review.

#### Distinguish the process purpose

Nickel plating deposits a coating, while stainless passivation addresses the stainless surface through a different process. These are not interchangeable names for polishing. Describe the required appearance, environment, friction or other function so the treatment discussion follows a defined need.

Working on this type of part? Explore our custom metal screws and include the functional requirements in your RFQ.

#### Consider dimensional and assembly effects

Plating thickness, exposed surfaces and thread fit may need control. For either route, specify any cleaning, masking or subsequent operation that affects the final condition. Surface treatment should be coordinated with the part drawing rather than added as an informal note after machining.

#### Agree evidence and acceptance

Request the appropriate process records and checks for the actual specification. Appearance approval can be useful but does not replace technical acceptance. If a reference sample is used, identify what it controls and which material or dimensional requirements remain governed by the drawing.

#### Specification example

If a buyer requests a silver finish, clarify whether the priority is visual consistency, corrosion behavior or another property. The answer can lead to a different process specification even when the parts look similar.

#### RFQ checklist

Substrate grade and condition

Required surface function

Treatment specification

Dimensional and masking requirements

Appearance and process acceptance

### What to specify for a zinc-flake coated custom screw
Source: https://precision-custom-fasteners-yang.boldshrew261.chatgpt.site/blog/zinc-flake-coating-specification/
Last modified: 2026-10-29

MATERIALS & FINISHES / 2 MIN READ

### What to specify for a zinc-flake coated custom screw

A coating-family name does not define the complete supplied surface. Custom fastener RFQs should connect the coating system with fit, friction and acceptance requirements.

By Theo Wan • ZUFEK Technical Editorial • Published October 29, 2026 Coatings & Surface Treatments

IN THIS GUIDE Identify the complete system Review the base material and pretreatment Include thread and bearing behavior Write measurable acceptance requirements RELATED PRODUCT Custom Flange Screws ↗

#### Identify the complete system

State the required coating specification and any topcoat, sealer or lubricant condition. A trade name alone can leave several technical choices unresolved. Make clear which requirements are mandatory and which can be proposed for review during quotation.

#### Review the base material and pretreatment

Consider the material condition and the complete treatment route, including cleaning and preparation. A non-electrolytic deposition step is not permission to ignore other process risks. Any hydrogen-related requirements should follow the applicable material and coating specification rather than an assumption based on appearance.

Working on this type of part? Explore our custom flange screws and include the functional requirements in your RFQ.

#### Include thread and bearing behavior

Coating can affect the fit and assembly conditions. Identify threads, seating faces and other functional surfaces, and state any friction-related requirements that the joint design uses. A corrosion requirement and a tightening requirement are different acceptance topics and should be documented separately.

#### Write measurable acceptance requirements

Where corrosion testing is required, specify the agreed method and criterion. Do not translate a test duration directly into a field-life guarantee. Include thickness, appearance, fit and process documentation as appropriate to the actual component and the supplied condition.

#### Specification example

For a high-strength flange screw, supply the mechanical requirement and the selected surface system together. This lets the supplier review pretreatment, final thread checks and any specified friction condition as one route.

#### RFQ checklist

Coating and topcoat specification

Base-material condition

Pretreatment requirements

Thread fit and assembly behavior

Agreed coating acceptance tests

QUALITY / 2 MIN READ

### Technical cleanliness: writing a useful fastener requirement

Cleanliness becomes a technical requirement when contamination can affect the assembly. Define what needs to be removed, how it is measured and how the clean condition is protected.

By Theo Wan • ZUFEK Technical Editorial • Published October 29, 2026 Cleaning, Locking & Assembly

IN THIS GUIDE Describe the contamination concern Agree the method and acceptance criteria Separate deburring from cleaning Protect the result through handling RELATED PRODUCT Hollow & Through-Hole Screws ↗

#### Describe the contamination concern

Explain whether particles could block a passage, damage a contact surface or affect another assembly function. Identify internal bores, thread roots and other areas that matter. A generic clean-and-dry instruction does not communicate a particle limit or a verified extraction method.

#### Agree the method and acceptance criteria

If a recognized cleanliness framework is required, specify the applicable procedure and project criteria. State the surfaces, extraction approach, reporting and acceptance limits relevant to the part. A standard number by itself does not define all of these choices for a particular order.

Working on this type of part? Explore our hollow & through-hole screws and include the functional requirements in your RFQ.

#### Separate deburring from cleaning

Attached burrs and loose residue are different conditions. The manufacturing route should address edge condition before the agreed cleaning process. Inspection may need to evaluate both, especially at cross holes and internal intersections where visual access is limited.

#### Protect the result through handling

Define drying, handling and packaging appropriate to the requirement. Recontamination can occur after cleaning if the process and packing sequence are not coordinated. Include the expected condition at delivery and any restrictions on protective oil or other residues.

#### Specification example

For an adhesive-dispensing passage, provide the smallest relevant flow section and the contamination acceptance requirement. A cleaning process can then be reviewed against the actual passage rather than a general appearance target.

#### RFQ checklist

Functional contamination concern

Specified surfaces and passages

Extraction and acceptance method

Permitted residues and dryness

Handling and packaging controls

PROCUREMENT / 2 MIN READ

### Pre-applied locking patches: what the screw drawing should say

A pre-applied locking feature needs a defined material, location and assembly requirement. A colored patch shown in a photograph is not a complete specification.

By Theo Wan • ZUFEK Technical Editorial • Published October 29, 2026 Cleaning, Locking & Assembly

IN THIS GUIDE Identify the locking system Define the application area Describe assembly and service conditions Agree the verification and handling RELATED PRODUCT Custom Metal Screws ↗

#### Identify the locking system

Nylon-type patches and adhesive-based systems use different mechanisms. State the approved system or provide the functional requirements for a proposal. Avoid treating every pre-applied material as the same product simply because it appears as a patch on the thread.

#### Define the application area

Specify location, coverage and any surfaces that must remain clear. Include thread length and the intended mating engagement. A patch applied to the wrong zone may not interact with the mating component in the same way as the approved sample or assembly.

Working on this type of part? Explore our custom metal screws and include the functional requirements in your RFQ.

#### Describe assembly and service conditions

State the intended mating material, installation process, exposure conditions and any reuse requirement. These inputs help the supplier review compatibility. Do not assume a locking feature establishes the joint clamp load or eliminates the need to define the tightening method.

#### Agree the verification and handling

Where torque behavior is required, define the test method and acceptance conditions. Include packaging and handling restrictions that protect the applied feature. Records should distinguish the base screw specification from the additional locking process so repeat orders preserve both.

#### Specification example

For a screw with a short working engagement, show where the mating thread sits in the installed condition. This helps ensure the specified patch zone actually overlaps the intended interface.

#### RFQ checklist

Approved locking system

Patch position and coverage

Mating thread and engagement

Assembly and reuse conditions

Torque behavior and handling criteria

### Preassembled washer screws: specify the complete set

A preassembled screw is supplied as a small assembly. The washer, retention method and component sequence need the same control as the screw itself.

By Theo Wan • ZUFEK Technical Editorial • Published October 29, 2026 Cleaning, Locking & Assembly

IN THIS GUIDE Define every supplied component Show the stack order and retention Review treatment and material compatibility Inspect the delivered assembly RELATED PRODUCT Custom Flange Screws ↗

#### Define every supplied component

Identify the screw, plain or spring washer, seal or other retained element by drawing or controlled specification. Include the material and finish of each component. A general note to add a washer can leave dimensions and properties unresolved.

#### Show the stack order and retention

Provide a section or assembly view showing the sequence and which elements are retained before installation. Explain the required freedom of movement. The manufacturing route should establish how components are assembled and held without damaging threads or functional surfaces.

Working on this type of part? Explore our custom flange screws and include the functional requirements in your RFQ.

#### Review treatment and material compatibility

Heat treatment, coating and cleaning may need to occur before or after assembly depending on the components. Seals and coated washers can introduce restrictions. Confirm the sequence for the approved set rather than assuming a process suitable for the bare screw is suitable for every assembled element.

#### Inspect the delivered assembly

Acceptance can include component presence, correct order, retention and the specified dimensional or functional checks. Keep these separate from the screw thread inspection. Packaging should protect the assembly condition and make it practical to confirm that the complete set was supplied.

#### Specification example

For a screw carrying an O-ring and washer, provide the assembled section and the permitted retention condition. This allows the quotation to account for both the metal part and the handling of the sealing element.

#### RFQ checklist

Component list and specifications

Stack order and movement

Retention method

Treatment and cleaning sequence

Delivered-assembly acceptance

### What CCD vision inspection can check on a custom screw
Source: https://precision-custom-fasteners-yang.boldshrew261.chatgpt.site/blog/ccd-screw-dimension-inspection/
Last modified: 2026-10-29

QUALITY / 3 MIN READ

### What CCD vision inspection can check on a custom screw

Camera-based dimensional inspection can evaluate visible features of a screw, but the image, setup and inspection program must match the requirement. It is one part of a complete acceptance plan.

By Theo Wan • ZUFEK Technical Editorial • Published October 29, 2026 CCD Vision & Dimensional Inspection

IN THIS GUIDE Choose the visible features to measure Review presentation and lighting Recognize what the image does not establish Validate and maintain the inspection program Validate presentation and edge visibility Define coverage and reject handling Pair optical checks with the missing methods RELATED PRODUCT Shoulder & Step Screws ↗

#### Choose the visible features to measure

Overall length, head diameter and stepped external profiles can be useful targets for optical checks when they are presented clearly. Identify the actual drawing characteristics rather than requesting a generic camera inspection with no defined measurements or acceptance limits.

#### Review presentation and lighting

Stable support, suitable optics and controlled lighting help produce consistent edges. Backlighting is useful for silhouette-based checks, while other surface features may require a different lighting arrangement. Establish the inspection view for the part rather than assuming one image reveals every characteristic.

Working on this type of part? Explore our shoulder & step screws and include the functional requirements in your RFQ.

#### Recognize what the image does not establish

A visible outline does not prove material grade, hardness or internal features hidden from the camera. Thread functional acceptance may require the specified gauges or other methods. The inspection plan should identify complementary checks instead of presenting one camera station as complete evidence of every requirement.

#### Validate and maintain the inspection program

Agree the measurement setup, acceptance limits, reference parts and any checks used to confirm consistent operation. Document changes to part revision or finish that may affect the image. Inspection coverage and handling of rejected parts should be defined for the actual order.

#### Validate presentation and edge visibility

Review part orientation, lighting, contrast and focus for each intended characteristic. Compare the programmed result with a suitable reference measurement using representative parts. Do not transfer a setup unchanged to a different coating, shape or presentation without checking whether the relevant edge is still detected appropriately.

#### Define coverage and reject handling

Document which external features the system evaluates and which are outside the validated program. Agree how borderline and rejected parts are handled, how setup changes are controlled and what record is retained. A pass indication is evidence only for the characteristics and conditions actually evaluated, not for every requirement on the drawing.

#### Pair optical checks with the missing methods

Use appropriate complementary checks for internal passages, thread acceptance, surface texture and material properties. A silhouette may show part of a thread outline without establishing the complete thread fit. Mitutoyo’s vision-measurement guide describes optical edge detection and alignment; the production inspection plan must still establish applicability to the actual screw.

#### Specification example

For a shoulder screw, define head diameter, shoulder length and overall length as separate checks. Then specify how the thread and any internal drive requirements are verified outside that silhouette measurement.

#### RFQ checklist

Drawing characteristics and limits

Required views and presentation

Calibration and reference checks

Complementary gauges or tests

Coverage and reject-handling plan

### First-article approval for custom screws: a practical handoff
Source: https://precision-custom-fasteners-yang.boldshrew261.chatgpt.site/blog/first-article-custom-screw-approval/

QUALITY / 2 MIN READ

### First-article approval for custom screws: a practical handoff

A sample is most useful when its identity, revision and acceptance scope are clear. First-article planning connects the approved drawing with the evidence needed before the next production decision.

By Theo Wan • ZUFEK Technical Editorial • Published October 29, 2026 CCD Vision & Dimensional Inspection

IN THIS GUIDE Link the sample to a controlled specification Define the evidence before making parts Separate visual and functional approval Close the feedback loop RELATED PRODUCT Custom Metal Screws ↗

#### Link the sample to a controlled specification

Record drawing number, revision, material condition and finish. Identify any agreed deviations separately. A loose sample with no revision history can create confusion if it is later used as a master for a repeat order or a manufacturing change.

#### Define the evidence before making parts

Agree which dimensions, material documents, process records and functional checks are required. The sample plan should follow the actual risk and acceptance requirements. Waiting until parts arrive to request additional tests can delay approval or require another manufacturing batch.

Working on this type of part? Explore our custom metal screws and include the functional requirements in your RFQ.

#### Separate visual and functional approval

Appearance, tool fit and trial assembly can reveal useful information, but they do not replace all drawing checks. Record what each review establishes and who accepts it. If a mating fixture is used, identify its revision and relevant condition as part of the approval record.

#### Close the feedback loop

Document changes arising from the review and decide whether they require a new drawing revision or another sample. Preserve an approved reference only with a clear record of what it controls. Production release should refer to the final agreed specification rather than an informal message chain.

#### Specification example

If a trial assembly leads to a longer shoulder, revise the drawing and identify the replacement sample. Keeping the original sample as an unexplained master can reintroduce the superseded dimension on a later order.

#### RFQ checklist

Drawing revision and sample identity

Required dimensional report

Material and process evidence

Defined assembly or appearance checks

Recorded approval and change disposition

### Sampling and 100% inspection: choosing the right coverage
Source: https://precision-custom-fasteners-yang.boldshrew261.chatgpt.site/blog/sampling-vs-full-fastener-inspection/
Last modified: 2026-10-29

QUALITY / 2 MIN READ

### Sampling and 100% inspection: choosing the right coverage

Inspection coverage should follow the characteristic and acceptance plan. Saying that a non-standard screw needs full inspection leaves the method, features and evidence undefined.

By Theo Wan • ZUFEK Technical Editorial • Published October 29, 2026 CCD Vision & Dimensional Inspection

IN THIS GUIDE Classify the characteristics Define what full inspection means Agree sampling as a documented plan Keep process control and acceptance connected RELATED PRODUCT Multi-Step & Multi-Shoulder Screws ↗

#### Classify the characteristics

Identify critical, functional and other drawing requirements through the responsible quality process. Explain the consequence of a nonconforming feature. This provides a basis for discussing which characteristics need screening and which can use the agreed sampling or approval method.

#### Define what full inspection means

Specify the feature, method and handling for every-piece screening. A camera check of length does not mean every thread, material property and internal surface has been verified. Destructive tests also cannot be applied to each delivered component in the same way as a non-destructive dimensional check.

Working on this type of part? Explore our multi-step & multi-shoulder screws and include the functional requirements in your RFQ.

#### Agree sampling as a documented plan

Where sampling is used, define the applicable procedure and order-specific acceptance requirements. Avoid an informal percentage with no lot definition or disposition rule. The plan should explain what happens when a sampled result fails and how the affected material is controlled.

#### Keep process control and acceptance connected

Inspection is more effective when supported by stable manufacturing and traceable records. Define reference checks, measurement capability and lot handling as appropriate. Additional inspection should address an identified requirement rather than simply adding a broad label that neither side can demonstrate.

#### Specification example

A buyer may request every-piece optical length screening while using separate thread-gauge sampling and material documentation. Writing each requirement explicitly is clearer than calling the entire order fully inspected.

#### RFQ checklist

Characteristic classification

Method and actual coverage

Lot definition and sampling rules

Failure disposition

Records and traceability

### Thread gauges and custom screw acceptance
Source: https://precision-custom-fasteners-yang.boldshrew261.chatgpt.site/blog/thread-gauge-acceptance-plan/

QUALITY / 2 MIN READ

### Thread gauges and custom screw acceptance

Thread acceptance begins with the specified thread system and fit. The gauge, supplied finish and inspection method should all refer to that same requirement.

By Theo Wan • ZUFEK Technical Editorial • Published October 29, 2026 Thread Rolling, Cutting & Tapping

IN THIS GUIDE Confirm the complete thread designation Agree the inspection condition Understand the scope of the check Control the inspection reference RELATED PRODUCT Fine & Extra-Fine Pitch Screws ↗

#### Confirm the complete thread designation

State the system, diameter, pitch, tolerance class and handedness. Include usable length and any special profile requirement. A gauge selected only from nominal diameter may not correspond to the pitch or fit that the drawing actually requires.

#### Agree the inspection condition

Determine whether acceptance refers to the final coated thread or another specifically defined stage. Surface condition and permitted residues should be considered in the inspection method. Records need to show which condition was checked rather than leaving the customer to infer it from the manufacturing sequence.

Working on this type of part? Explore our fine & extra-fine pitch screws and include the functional requirements in your RFQ.

#### Understand the scope of the check

A functional gauge check addresses defined thread acceptance, but it does not automatically verify every profile detail, material property or external shoulder. Special features may need additional dimensional or profile inspection. Specify those checks separately when the function requires them.

#### Control the inspection reference

Use gauges and methods appropriate to the thread specification and maintain the required control of the inspection equipment. If a special mating component is used for a trial, distinguish that assembly check from formal thread acceptance. Both can be useful without being interchangeable.

#### Specification example

For two fine-pitch ends on one stud, identify the gauge requirement for end A and end B separately. This avoids treating a successful check at one end as evidence for the complete part.

#### RFQ checklist

Thread system, pitch and class

Final supplied condition

Appropriate gauge and method

Additional special-profile checks

Inspection equipment and records
